{"type":"text","timestamp":1794624741950,"sessionID":"ses_e2809389dffea4lyHY3oNbpjlO","part":{"id":"prt_1d7f86233001NtW0ROKQlxbOvE","messageID":"msg_1d7f842c9001HkF9suUqhC0vYW","sessionID":"ses_e2809389dffea4lyHY3oNbpjlO","type":"text","text":"The episode is over, and the rover very likely ran out of battery at the last tick. If it did, the score is 0.\n\n**What went right:** all 7 targets were sampled: 5 at the start (t1–t5) and the 2 that appeared mid-mission (d1, d2). Six were sampled before their deadlines. d2 was sampled at tick 24, after its tick-18 deadline, so it counts for a quarter of its value. That is 9.5 of a possible 12.\n\n**What went wrong:** I ran out of energy. I filled the command queue many ticks ahead and never checked the battery against the full 50-tick idle drain (0.5 per tick). By the time I worked it out, at tick 17, the drives and the sample needed to reach d2 were already queued, and queued commands can't be cancelled. After the d2 sample at tick 24 the battery was 12.7. The remaining 26 ticks of idle drain cost 13.0, even without moving. Driving the 4.3 m back to base would have used up the battery even sooner, so the only option was to stay put.\n\n**Final state:** the last packet I received was for tick 47, showing 1.2 battery. At that rate it would be 0.2 at tick 49 and −0.3 at tick 50. The rover finished about 4.3 m from base, outside the 0.75 m base radius. If the final tick isn't charged, it ends alive with 0.2 and gets half value: 4.75 of 12, about 0.40. I haven't confirmed which way it went.\n\n**What would have avoided it:** checking the battery budget, including the idle drain to the end, before committing to a new target. Here that meant going straight from d1 back to base and skipping the late d2 sample. That would have ended at base with about 5 battery left, for a score of 9/12 = 0.75.","time":{"start":1794624741939,"end":1794624741948}}}
